Fit the monotone curve

Source: R/fit_ms.R
fit_ms.Rd

Monotone B-spline equation of the digital measure by monotonic likelihood boosting (Leitenstorfer and Tutz 2007, GMBBoost; the default) or by Ramsay's (1988) monotone regression splines (`curve = "ispline"`), in one of three ways (the boosting steps, tuning values and stopping rule are the same):

Usage

fit_ms(
  grm,
  Y,
  sqi,
  mode = c("fixed", "joint", "eap"),
  lambda = 20,
  shrinkage = 0.1,
  max_iter = 10000,
  patience = 100,
  criterion = "AIC",
  item_every = 5,
  hetero = TRUE,
  curve = c("boost", "ispline"),
  n_knots = "AIC",
  max_knots = 5,
  order = 2,
  family = c("gaussian", "poisson", "negbin")
)

Arguments

grm

output of [fit_grm()] on the same items

Y

item responses (0..3, NA allowed), n x J

sqi

the digital measure, length n (non-increasing in eta)

mode

"fixed" (MS-Fixed), "joint" (MS-Joint) or "eap" (MS-EAP)

lambda

ridge penalty of the fitting step (default 20)

shrinkage

step length nu (default 0.1)

max_iter

maximum number of boosting iterations

patience

stop when the AIC has not improved for this many iterations

criterion

"AIC" (default) or "BIC" for the stopping iteration

item_every

MS-Joint: item M-step every this many iterations

hetero

TRUE (default) for log sigma(eta) = g0 + g1 eta, FALSE for a constant residual SD (sensitivity analysis)

curve

"boost" (default): monotonic likelihood boosting of the 24-coefficient B-spline, as above. "ispline": Ramsay's (1988) monotone regression spline, \(\mu(\eta) = \beta_0 - \sum_m a_m I_m(\eta)\), \(a_m \ge 0\), with I-splines of order `order` on `n_knots` interior knots at quantiles of N(0, 1) (see [ispline_knots()]), fitted by maximum likelihood under the bounds (EM over the nodes for "fixed" and "joint", direct for "eap"). The three ways of handling the latent trait are the same. `lambda`, `shrinkage`, `patience` and `item_every` are then unused, and `max_iter` caps the EM iterations.

n_knots

`curve = "ispline"`: number of interior knots, or "AIC" (default) to choose among 0 to `max_knots` by `criterion`

max_knots

largest number of interior knots tried

order

I-spline order k (default 2, piecewise quadratic I-splines, so the curve is a quadratic spline with continuous slope)

family

distribution of the digital measure given the latent trait. "gaussian" (default): a continuous measure (actigraphy index, gait speed, distance), normal with the mean curve and a constant or log-linear SD. "poisson" or "negbin" (negative binomial, Var = mu + mu^2 / theta): a count measure (daily steps, events, deaths); the spline is then fitted on the log scale, log E[y | eta] = f(eta) non-increasing, by the GLM version of the boosting (Leitenstorfer and Tutz 2007: penalised Fisher-scoring steps with the Fisher weights of the family, deviance-based split choice and AIC stop) or by the I-spline ML fit. theta is estimated by ML along the way. `hetero` applies to "gaussian" only. For count families the approximate hat matrix is accumulated on the units (nodes or persons) with the current Fisher weights, and [ms_vcov()] is not available; use [ms_bootstrap()]. "poisson" suits small counts (deaths, events). A large Poisson count (mean in the thousands) locates the latent trait more finely than the 61 quadrature nodes resolve, which biases the curve; fit_ms() warns when this happens. Large counts such as daily steps are overdispersed anyway and should use "negbin".

Value

list(a, d, act, mode, converged, iter, iter_aic, iter_bic, df, stop_reason, path, item_ll (not for "eap"), R_coef (coefficient operator at the AIC stop, used by [ms_vcov()]), eta_cov (EAP scores, "eap" only), curve). For `curve = "ispline"`, `iter` is the number of EM iterations, `path` the knot selection table, `R_coef` NULL, and the result also has n_knots, knots, order and coef (beta0 and the I-spline coefficients).

Details

"fixed" MS-Fixed. Items held at the GRM estimates. Each iteration: E-step (posterior p(eta_q | C_i, SQI_i) on the nodes), sigma update, one boosting step on the posterior-weighted node totals. "joint" MS-Joint. As "fixed", but each iteration also takes an M-step for the item parameters from the same posterior (expected category counts per node), so the items and the curve are estimated together and the latent scale is defined by the PSQI and the SQI jointly. Items start at the GRM estimates. The item M-step is taken every `item_every` iterations (default 5); skipping it in between keeps every iteration a generalised EM step, and the items settle long before the AIC stop. "eap" MS-EAP. The EAP scores from the PSQI-only GRM are treated as the covariate: the paper's algorithm exactly as published (observed covariate, normal response).

Residual SD: with hetero = TRUE (default) log sigma(eta) = g0 + g1 eta. The sigma step then updates (g0, g1) by Newton steps on the posterior-expected (MS-EAP: observed) log-likelihood given the curve, units are weighted by 1 / sigma_u^2 in the fitting step, and (g0, g1) are not counted in tr(H_l) (their number is fixed, so the AIC minimum does not move). With hetero = FALSE sigma is constant, with its closed-form update.

Stopping: AIC(l) = Dev_l + 2 tr(H_l), H_l = I - (I - M_l)...(I - M_0) the approximate hat matrix of the person-level fitted values (paper eq. 11). Dev_l is -2 log L(C, SQI) with eta integrated out ("fixed", "joint") or -2 log L(SQI | EAP) ("eap"). For "joint" the 28 item parameters are not counted in tr(H_l); their number is the same at every iteration, so the AIC minimum does not move. Search stops when the AIC has not improved for `patience` iterations, no monotone split exists, or max_iter.

References

Leitenstorfer F, Tutz G (2007). Generalized monotonic regression based on B-splines with an application to air pollution data. Biostatistics 8, 654-673.

Ramsay JO (1988). Monotone regression splines in action. Statistical Science 3, 425-461.
